question.text: Will Dan S. Sullivan publicly concede Alaska's 2026 U.S. Senate race by November 27, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Dan S. Sullivan — the Republican incumbent U.S. Senator for Alaska — publicly concedes defeat in Alaska's 2026 U.S. Senate election at any time by 11:59 p.m. UTC on November 27, 2026, and NO otherwise (including if Sullivan is instead certified as the election's winner). A qualifying concession is a public statement by Sullivan himself, or by his campaign or an authorised spokesperson on his behalf, acknowledging that he has lost the election and/or that Mary Peltola (or any other rival candidate) has won it. Statements that only note that ballots are still being counted, that the campaign is awaiting final results or certification, or that decline to comment do not qualify. Resolution will be based on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print: A concession that is later retracted, or that is followed by a recount request or an election contest, still counts. A hedged or conditional acknowledgment (for example, congratulating Peltola "if these results hold") does not qualify unless and until Sullivan states that he has lost. A concession reported second-hand (for example, the Peltola campaign saying Sullivan called to congratulate her) counts only if Sullivan or his campaign confirms it.

research:
Sullivan has not conceded as of today, 17 November. His campaign said on 16 November that it would wait until every legal vote is "counted and certified", and also that it would "have more to say by the end of this week." Certification is targeted for 25 November, two days before this question closes on the 27th.

## 1. Resolution source
- No official tally decides this question. It resolves on credible reports of a concession by Sullivan or his campaign. The vote count only matters for timing.
- 2026-11-17: I couldn't read the Division of Elections summary report because it is a PDF my tools can't open, and I found no CSV or JSON version. [ElectionSummaryReportRPT.pdf](https://www.elections.alaska.gov/enr/26GENR/results/ElectionSummaryReportRPT.pdf)
- 2026-11-16: According to Newsweek, the latest count had Peltola at 141,637 first-choice votes (50.0%) and Sullivan at 130,162 (45.9%), a gap of 11,475. The AP put the count at about 98% complete. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/dan-sullivan-breaks-silence-as-alaska-senate-race-nears-showdown-12725062)
- Other outlets give Peltola 49.98% to Sullivan's 45.93% as of 16 November. That leaves her just short of 50%, so ranked-choice tabulation would be needed. [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/us/democrat-close-to-majority-in-alaska-us-senate-race-as-ballot-processing-nears-end-6125861)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-16: Campaign spokesperson Nate Adams said: "we will let that process run its course until every legal vote is counted and certified... We will not be commenting on individual ballot updates or outside projections in the meantime." [Democracy Docket](https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/sen-dan-sullivan-campaign-says-it-wont-concede-alaska-senate-race-until-its-certified/)
- The same Facebook post said the campaign would "have more to say by the end of this week." Sullivan "is grateful to the Alaskans who made their voices heard, and he remains focused on his work for our state." It was the first post about the race from either Sullivan Facebook account since election night. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/dan-sullivan-breaks-silence-as-alaska-senate-race-nears-showdown-12725062)
- Nothing settles the question yet. I found no statement dated 17 November.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Trump called the race a "disgrace." He also posted that votes for "the Fake Dan Sullivan" should go to the senator. The administration's criminal investigation into whether the Peltola campaign helped put the second Sullivan on the ballot is continuing. [Democracy Docket live](https://democracydocket.com/news-alerts/live-updates-alaska-senate-race-heads-for-democratic-win-amid-trump-threats)
- 2026-11-15: NBC's Decision Desk projected Peltola is "likely" to win, with at least 95% confidence. The AP has not called the race. [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrat-mary-peltola-likely-win-alaska-senate-race-rcna608673)
- 2026-11-14: Peltola declared victory. [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/nov/14/peltola-declares-victory-alaska-senate-race/)
- 2026-11-14: Peltola led 138,240 to 127,828 (a 10,412-vote gap) with about 96% counted. [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273838/20261114/peltola-leads-sullivan-10412-last-uncalled-senate-race.htm)
- The Justice Department's appeal at the Ninth Circuit is still pending, and the department has not asked for an injunction blocking certification. [Democracy Docket](https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/sen-dan-sullivan-campaign-says-it-wont-concede-alaska-senate-race-until-its-certified/)

## 4. Base rates (recent Alaska statewide losers)
- 2022-11-23: Kelly Tshibaka conceded to Murkowski in writing on the day the ranked-choice tabulation finished, about three weeks after the election. She had earlier hinted she might challenge the results, and her statement attacked ranked-choice voting. [Must Read Alaska](https://mustreadalaska.com/tshibaka-concedes-with-grace-to-murkowski-who-wins-with-over-50-for-first-time-in-her-history-thanks-to-open-primaries), [ADN](https://adn.com/politics/2022/11/23/alaska-us-sen-lisa-murkowski-wins-reelection)
- The following are from memory and I did not check them:
  - 2024: Peltola conceded the House race to Nick Begich around 20 November, roughly when the AP called it and before the ranked-choice tabulation.
  - 2014: Mark Begich conceded to Sullivan on about 17 November, several days after the AP call.
  - 2020: Al Gross conceded shortly after the AP call.
- Taken together, Alaska statewide losers have usually conceded within about one day to one week of an AP call or the tabulation. That would put a concession before 27 November.
- Factors pointing the other way:
  - Sullivan has explicitly tied any concession to certification.
  - Trump and the Justice Department are contesting the result.
  - The recount deadline (30 November) and election-contest deadline (5 December) fall after the question closes.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-11-17, Polymarket "Alaska Senate Election Winner": Peltola 99.85%, Sullivan 0.05%.
- 2026-11-17, Kalshi margin of victory: Peltola by 3-6% at 98%.
- 2026-11-17, Kalshi Senate control: Democrats 99.9%.
- I found no market on whether or when Sullivan will concede. The markets above price who wins, not whether he concedes.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **2026-11-18:** The 15-day deadline for overseas ballots. The final count and any ranked-choice tabulation happen the same day. If Peltola ends at 50% or more, no tabulation is needed. An AP call is likely around this point. [mlq.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/peltola-leads-alaskas-senate-race-with-4998-as-the-final-count-and-any-ranked-choice-tabulation-arrive-wednesday/)
- **By about 2026-11-20 to 11-22:** The campaign's promised end-of-week statement. This could be a concession, a challenge, or a decision to keep waiting.
- **2026-11-25:** Target date for certification. This is the campaign's own stated condition for saying more, and it leaves two days before the question closes.
- **Ninth Circuit (No. 26-7304):** The intervenors' motion for summary affirmance is pending. The department has not sought an injunction, so there is no court block on certification so far.
- **2026-11-30 and 2026-12-05:** The recount and election-contest deadlines, both after the question closes. A concession followed by a recount request would still count as YES.
- **Possible pressure from Trump:** He may urge Sullivan not to concede.

If certification slips, or if he waits for the recount window (requests due about 2026-11-30) or the contest window (2026-12-05), that pushes past the deadline.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 10 days remain, until 27 Nov 23:59 UTC. Yes requires Sullivan or his campaign to publicly acknowledge that he lost or that Peltola won. Hedged or "awaiting certification" statements do not count. The likely triggers are the 18 Nov final count and tabulation, the campaign's promised end-of-week statement (around 20 to 22 Nov), and certification, targeted for 25 Nov.

**(b) Status quo.** Sullivan has not conceded. On 16 Nov his campaign said it will wait until every vote is "counted and certified." If nothing changed, the answer would be No.

**(c) Base rate.** Recent Alaska statewide losers conceded within about a day of the ranked-choice tabulation or the AP call, all well before certification:
- Tshibaka, 2022, on tabulation day.
- Peltola, 2024, on tabulation day.
- Begich, 2014.
- Gross, 2020.

That is roughly 4 of 4 conceding within three weeks of the election. Nationally, most clearly beaten Senate incumbents concede within about one to two weeks. The base rate for conceding inside this window is about 80 to 85%.
